mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved monotonically for four weeks (from -24.1 to -15.7) and every point of transit recovery mechanically lifts footfall in transit-adjacent retail corridors; RETAIL_REC therefore keeps climbing over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose 8.4 points across the four weeks ending 2022-02-15
failure_condition: The next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is equal to or below its last-28-day mean (-19.0) while TRANSIT continues to improve.

mechanism_narrative: Once the WORKPLACES weekly mean crosses above -15 percent, office attendance reaches the density needed to restore weekday commuter footfall, and downtown retail-and-recreation activity rises within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -20.0 to -14.3 over the four weeks ending 2022-02-15
failure_condition: In the two weeks after WORKPLACES prints above -15.0, RETAIL_REC weekly means fail to exceed their level in the week before the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT recovery and above-baseline PARKS activity interact: transit normality restores multi-stop trip chains while parks pull households out of the home, and their combination generates more discretionary retail trips than either series produces alone.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean at or above +5 while TRANSIT improves week-on-week
failure_condition: In weeks when PARKS is at or above +5 and TRANSIT improves, RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days shows no larger gain than in weeks when TRANSIT improves without PARKS support.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-surge normalization regime, elevated GROCERY_PHARM (+9.0) reflects residual pantry-loading and pharmacy trips; as that series normalizes toward baseline, household time and spend reallocate to discretionary retail, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM averaged +8.0 over the four weeks ending 2022-02-15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the four weeks in which GROCERY_PHARM falls below +6.0.

mechanism_narrative: Continued PARKS expansion above +10 diverts discretionary leisure time and spending into open-air activity, substituting for indoor retail-and-recreation trips and stalling the RETAIL_REC recovery over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -9.3 to +8.4 before easing to +4.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-14-day mean stays above its last-14-day mean even after PARKS prints above +10.0.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of falling RESIDENTIAL (7.4 to 3.7) and rising TRANSIT is the cleanest signature of out-of-home normalization, and that combination produces a fast one-week lift in retail-and-recreation footfall.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls at least 1 point week-on-week while TRANSIT improves
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 7.4 to 3.7 while TRANSIT rose from -24.1 to -15.7
failure_condition: In weeks when RESIDENTIAL falls and TRANSIT rises together, RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to its value in the preceding week.

mechanism_narrative: Removal of capacity and closing-time limits raises TRANSIT and WORKPLACES together; because genuine policy easing is the only force that moves both series in lockstep, their joint multi-week improvement predicts a durable four-week retail recovery.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve by at least 3 points over two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improved in every week of the four-week window
failure_condition: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve by at least 3 points over two consecutive weeks yet RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean does not exceed its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Late-February seasonal daylight gain lifts PARKS and reshapes grocery-and-pharmacy trip timing; the accompanying spring rebound in outdoor-adjacent retail delivers a one-week positive impulse to RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved in each of the four weeks ending 2022-02-15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's mean over the next 7 days is equal to or below its mean over the last 7 days.
